title: Coinbase vs. Paypal: Two Fintech Giants, Two Very Different Price Tags. Which Stock Wins?
ai_summary: Coinbase and PayPal are compared on financials and valuations, with Coinbase showing faster revenue growth (9.4% vs 4.3%) but a higher valuation. PayPal trades at a lower P/E and P/S, offering a more attractive entry point. The author favors PayPal for long-term investors due to its lower valuation and established cash flow.

title: PayPal (NASDAQ:PYPL) Stock Price Expected to Rise, Truist Financial Analyst Says
ai_summary: Truist Financial raised its PayPal price target to $58 from $53, keeping a hold rating. Other analysts also adjusted targets, with an average rating of Hold and average target of $56.42. PayPal's stock closed at $57.25, down $0.28.

title: PayPal Is Down More Than 80% From Its Peak. Here's Why I Still Own It
ai_summary: PayPal's stock has fallen over 80% from its 2021 peak, and takeover talks have ended. The company reported 5% revenue growth and $1.8 billion in quarterly free cash flow, with an aggressive buyback program. The author holds shares, citing a 10x forward earnings multiple and potential double-digit EPS growth from buybacks.

title: LianLian Global taps PayPal, Venmo to streamline cross-border seller payouts (PYPL:NASDAQ)
ai_summary: LianLian Global announced a partnership with PayPal to enable payouts to PayPal and Venmo accounts for its social commerce, marketplace, and e-commerce clients. Brands are expected to spend $32.6 billion on creators in 2026, with PayPal holding over 400 million active accounts and Venmo reaching 67 million monthly active accounts.

title: PayPal Holdings (PYPL) Tests Its Undervalued Narrative After Glance Checkout Deal
ai_summary: PayPal Holdings integrated Glance's agentic commerce into its app, giving U.S. shoppers native PayPal checkout. The stock gained 8.78% in one month, but the author estimates a fair value of $68 versus a last close of $57.54, citing $6.8B annual free cash flow and 440M active accounts.

title: $5 trillion wiped out: What went wrong for PayPal, Nike, Adobe and other global giants?
ai_summary: Between August 2021 and September 2026, 172 of the world's 1,000 largest companies lost $4.96 trillion in market capitalization, according to BestBrokers. PayPal led with an 85.41% drop, followed by Nike and Adobe, while pandemic-era firms like Zoom and BioNTech also fell sharply.

title: Krak vs. PayPal vs. Cash App: Fees, Reach and Bank Withdrawals
ai_summary: Cash App requires US residency, while Krak and PayPal support US-to-UK personal payments. Conversion and bank withdrawal terms determine the cost beyond the in-app transfer.
